question: Which of the following is not an increased risk in multiple pregnancy?
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: Which of the following is not an increased risk in multiple pregnancy? 


###Options:
A.  Placenta praevia.
B.  Diabetes mellitus.
C.  Pre-eclampsia.
D.  Malpresentation.
E.  Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR).

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: B. Diabetes mellitus.

Rationale:  
Multiple (twin or higher‐order) pregnancies are characteristically associated with a larger placental mass and limited intra-uterine space; as a result they carry higher rates of:

• Pre-eclampsia – the larger placental mass increases the likelihood of hypertensive disease.  
• Placenta praevia – a larger area of implantation makes low-lying placentation more common.  
• Malpresentation – at least one fetus is often breech, transverse or oblique because of restricted room.  
• Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR) – competition for nutrients and placental insufficiency limit fetal growth.

By contrast, the incidence of diabetes mellitus (whether pre-existing or gestational) is not significantly higher in multiple pregnancies than in singleton pregnancies, so it is the exception in this list.

Answer:

Key strategies to prevent acute diarrhoeal disease among mothers and children in Lagos State include:

1. Safe water
   • Expand municipal piped-water coverage and fix broken pipes.  
   • Encourage household treatment (boiling, chlorination, ceramic or sachet filters).  
   • Promote safe storage in narrow-neck, covered containers.

2. Sanitation
   • Support construction and proper use of improved latrines.  
   • Enforce regulations against open defecation and indiscriminate waste disposal.  
   • Ensure regular desludging of septic tanks and safe faecal-sludge management.

3. Hand-washing with soap
   • Teach mothers/caregivers to wash hands: after defecation, after cleaning a child, before food preparation, and before feeding a child.  
   • Install tippy-tap or running-water stations in homes, markets, schools and health centres.

4. Infant and young-child feeding
   • Promote exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months and continued breastfeeding up to 2 years.  
   • Discourage bottle-feeding; use cup-and-spoon if supplementation is needed.  
   • Introduce complementary foods after 6 months, prepared and stored hygienically.

5. Food hygiene
   • “Boil it, cook it, peel it or leave it.”  
   • Re-heat leftovers thoroughly; keep cooked food <2 hours at room temperature.  
   • Wash fruits/vegetables with safe water.

6. Vaccination
   • Ensure every infant receives rotavirus vaccine (now in Nigeria’s EPI).  
   • Maintain high measles coverage because measles predisposes to severe diarrhoea.

7. Micronutrient support
   • Provide routine vitamin A for children 6-59 months.  
   • Give preventive zinc (10–20 mg/day for 10–14 days) with every diarrhoea episode to shorten duration and reduce recurrence.

8. Prompt home management
   • Teach mothers to start oral rehydration solution (ORS) immediately a child develops loose stools and to continue feeding.  
   • Recognise danger signs (blood in stool, persistent vomiting, inability to drink, lethargy) and seek care early.

9. Environmental measures
   • Regular refuse collection to reduce flies.  
   • Drainage maintenance to prevent flooding and sewage contamination.  
   • Control street food safety through licensing and periodic inspection.

10. Behaviour-change communication
   • Use community health workers, radio, social media and religious gatherings to reinforce diarrhoea-prevention messages.  
   • Incorporate WASH education into antenatal, postnatal and immunisation clinics.

11. Policy and multisectoral action
   • Strengthen Lagos State WASH committees, integrate WASH indicators into primary-health-care supervision.  
   • Subsidise household water filters/latrines for poor urban and peri-urban communities.  
   • Engage private sector in water kiosks and sanitation marketing.

Together, these water-sanitation-hygiene (WASH) improvements, coupled with optimal breastfeeding, vaccination, micronutrient support and caregiver education, can markedly reduce the incidence and severity of acute diarrhoeal disease in mothers and children across Lagos State.

question: A thirty-seven-year-old woman attends for a routine dating scan. She asks you in detail what information will be obtained from the scan. Which of the following will not be possible?
C: The early detection of twin pregnancies.
D: The detection of a failed pregnancy.

###Question: A thirty-seven-year-old woman attends for a routine dating scan. She asks you in detail what information will be obtained from the scan. Which of the following will not be possible? 
 

###Options:
A.  Accurate dating of the pregnancy.
B.  The detection of placenta praevia.
C.  The early detection of twin pregnancies.
D.  The detection of a failed pregnancy.
E.  The detection of uterine abnormalities.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: B. The detection of placenta praevia.

Rationale:
A first-trimester “dating scan” (generally performed between 10–14 weeks) can:
• Measure the crown-rump length and give very accurate gestational dating (A).  
• Identify number of fetuses and chorionicity, therefore detecting twin (or higher) pregnancies early (C).  
• Demonstrate fetal cardiac activity and thus diagnose a failed or missed pregnancy (D).  
• Visualise the uterus and adnexa, so structural uterine abnormalities or fibroids can be seen (E).

Although the placental site can be noted, the placenta is still developing and its margin frequently “moves” away from the internal os as the uterus enlarges. A diagnosis of placenta praevia cannot be made reliably until after the mid-trimester anomaly scan (around 20 weeks). Hence, detection of placenta praevia is not possible at a routine early dating scan.

Correct option: D.  Attend hospital if fetal movements are decreased.

Rationale:  
After 28 weeks’ gestation the single most reliable early warning sign of fetal compromise is a reduction in maternal perception of fetal movements. Current RCOG guidance is that any woman who feels a decrease or cessation of movements should be advised to attend her maternity unit promptly for assessment (CTG ± ultrasound).  

• Auscultating the fetal heart at home offers only momentary reassurance and does not assess ongoing well-being.  
• Asking the woman to complete a 24-hour kick chart first may delay necessary assessment; formal routine kick-charts are no longer recommended.  
• Booking a growth scan within 48 hours is too slow if compromise is developing.  
• A nuchal translucency scan is a first-trimester test and irrelevant at 32 weeks.

Therefore the appropriate advice is to tell her to attend hospital immediately if she experiences decreased fetal movements.

question: A woman is found to have oligohydramnios at 30/40. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: A woman is found to have oligohydramnios at 30/40. Which of the following is the most likely cause? 


###Options:
A.  Duodenal atresia.
B.  Placental chorioangioma.
C.  Diabetes.
D.  Oesophageal atresia.
E.  Renal agenesis.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: E. Renal agenesis

Rationale:
The volume of amniotic fluid in the second and third trimesters is maintained primarily by fetal urine production and swallowing. Any condition that markedly decreases fetal urine output leads to oligohydramnios, whereas conditions that impair fetal swallowing or increase urine production cause polyhydramnios.

• Renal agenesis (or severe renal dysgenesis) results in absent or minimal fetal urine, so the liquor volume falls → oligohydramnios.  
• Duodenal atresia and oesophageal atresia prevent normal swallowing, therefore they are classically linked with polyhydramnios, not oligohydramnios.  
• Placental chorioangioma is a vascular placental tumour often associated with increased placental blood flow and polyhydramnios.  
• Maternal diabetes tends to cause fetal polyuria and polyhydramnios.

Thus the most likely cause of oligohydramnios at 30 weeks is renal agenesis.

C. Correct – The marked increase in plasma volume and cardiac output during early pregnancy produces a benign, soft ejection systolic flow murmur. This is audible in the majority of pregnant women; studies quote figures of about 80–90 % and it is commonly detectable from around 12 weeks’ (12/40) gestation.  

D. Incorrect – Symphysis–fundal height (SFH) measurement with a tape should begin once the uterus reaches the level of the umbilicus, i.e. at about 24 weeks, and be plotted at each visit thereafter, not from 16 weeks.  

E. Incorrect – Antenatal inspection or “pinching” of nipples does not reliably predict breastfeeding difficulties; nipple shape bears little relation to subsequent feeding success, and routine examination is not recommended.

###Answer:

• (E) is partly true—head-circumference measurements can be used for dating in the second trimester—but the key universally accepted fact for calculating an EDD is the 280-day (40-week) duration, making option C the most appropriate answer.

C.  Lanugo shedding.
D.  Thermoregulation due to thin skin.

###Answer:

Correct option: D. Thermoregulation due to thin skin.

Rationale:
Pre-term infants have an immature integumentary system. Their epidermis is very thin, the stratum corneum is poorly developed, and they possess little subcutaneous (insulating) fat. This combination results in rapid transepidermal water and heat loss, making maintenance of body temperature a major clinical problem in the neonatal unit.

• Option B is incorrect; vernix caseosa production peaks late in gestation, so premature babies actually tend to have less, not excessive, vernix.  
• Option C is incorrect; lanugo (fine fetal hair) is usually still present in pre-term infants and is shed closer to term, so shedding is not the principal problem.  
• Option E is incorrect because hair follicles develop early (by the end of the first trimester); their absence is not a typical issue in prematurity.

Therefore, the chief difficulty for a pre-term neonate is thermoregulation secondary to thin, immature skin.

###Question: Which best describes the reproductive history of a woman at 30 weeks gestation with a previous twin delivery and a Spontaneous termination of pregnancy at 27 weeks?






###Options:
A.  G3P3 +0.
B.  G3P1+1.
C.  G4P3+0.
D.  G4P2+1.
E.  G3P2+1.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: B. G3 P1 +1  

Rationale:  
• Gravida (G) is the total number of times the woman has been pregnant, including the current pregnancy.  
 – Previous twin pregnancy = 1  
 – Previous pregnancy that ended at 27 weeks = 1  
 – Present pregnancy (30 weeks) = 1  
 Total G = 3  

• Para (P) records pregnancies that reached the age of viability (in the traditional obstetric notation used in India, ≥28 weeks), irrespective of the number of babies or their outcome.  
 – The twin delivery occurred beyond viability, so it counts as one para.  
 – The 27-week loss occurred before 28 weeks, so it does NOT add to para.  
 Total P = 1  

• “+” (abortus) records pregnancies that ended before viability (<28 weeks).  
 – The spontaneous termination at 27 weeks therefore counts as one abortion.  
 Abortus = 1  

Hence the correct notation is G3 P1 +1.

question: A nineteen-year-old-girl is admitted with pelvic pain, a positive pregnancy test and a 3 cm viable ectopic pregnancy seen in the right fallopian tube on ultrasound. She has already had a left salpingectomy for a previous ectopic. The best management would be:

###Question: A nineteen-year-old-girl is admitted with pelvic pain, a positive pregnancy test and a 3 cm viable ectopic pregnancy seen in the right fallopian tube on ultrasound. She has already had a left salpingectomy for a previous ectopic. The best management would be:
 





###Options:
A.  Laparoscopic salpingectomy.
B.  Conservative management with serial βHCGs.
C.  Laparotomy.
D.  Laparoscopic salpingostomy
E.  Methotrexate.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Laparoscopic salpingostomy  

Rationale:  
• This woman has already lost her left tube to a previous ectopic, so preservation of the only remaining tube is crucial for future fertility.  
• The present ectopic is 3 cm and viable (fetal cardiac activity). The presence of cardiac activity and the size (>2 cm) markedly lower the success rate of medical treatment with methotrexate.  
• Expectant (conservative) management with serial β-hCGs is inappropriate because the pregnancy is viable and symptomatic (pelvic pain).  
• A salpingectomy (laparoscopic or by laparotomy) would remove her remaining tube and almost certainly render her infertile.  
• Therefore the optimal management is a fertility-preserving surgical approach: laparoscopic salpingostomy, which removes the ectopic gestation while leaving the tube in situ.

###Answer:

Rationale:  
Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) is produced by the granulosa cells of pre-antral and small antral follicles. question: Fetal and neonatal effects of Rhesus isoimmunisation include the following except

###Question: Fetal and neonatal effects of Rhesus isoimmunisation include the following except



###Options:
A.  Anencephaly.
B.  Kernicterus
C.  Hydrops fetalis
D.  Spontaneous abortion
E.  Intrauterine fetal death

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Anencephaly

Rationale:
Rhesus (Rh) isoimmunisation produces immune-mediated haemolysis of fetal red blood cells. Its consequences are all related to severe fetal/neonatal anaemia and subsequent hyperbilirubinaemia:

• In utero it can lead to hydrops fetalis and intra-uterine fetal death.  
• At birth or shortly afterwards it can cause marked jaundice that may progress to kernicterus.  
• Severe disease may even precipitate pregnancy loss that is sometimes described as a spontaneous abortion.

Rh isoimmunisation, however, does not cause structural congenital malformations. Neural-tube defects such as anencephaly arise from failure of neural-tube closure and are totally unrelated to haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn. Hence, anencephaly is the exception.

question: In a patient with breech presentation, the following are true except?

###Answer:

Correct option: E. Internal podalic version is indicated  

Rationale:  
• External cephalic version (ECV) is recommended at 36-37 weeks in an uncomplicated breech, so option A is true.  
• Selected women with a term singleton breech in favorable circumstances may be offered a trial of vaginal breech delivery, so option B is true.

• Breech is more common in conditions that prevent normal engagement, such as prematurity, placenta praevia, uterine anomalies and multiple pregnancy; hence multiple pregnancy is indeed a risk factor, making option D true.  
• Internal podalic version is used chiefly to convert a transverse lie (especially the second twin) to a breech for immediate extraction; it is not indicated for the routine management of a term singleton breech presentation. Therefore option E is the false statement (the “except” choice).

###Question: The following can be used as medical management of menorrhagia

B.  Intrauterine systems
C.  Intrauterine copper device
D.  Implanon
E.  DMPA

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct options: A, B, and E.

Rationale  
Heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia) can be treated medically with both non-hormonal and hormonal agents that reduce endometrial blood loss.

• Tranexamic acid (A) – an antifibrinolytic that decreases fibrinolysis in the endometrium and reduces menstrual blood loss by 40-60 %.  
• Levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (B) – delivers progestogen directly to the endometrium, causing marked endometrial thinning and is recommended as first-line therapy in many guidelines.  
• Depot medroxy-progesterone acetate, DMPA (E) – a long-acting progestogen injection that induces endometrial atrophy and often results in amenorrhoea over time.

In contrast:
• A copper intrauterine device (C) tends to increase menstrual bleeding and is therefore not used to treat menorrhagia.  
• Implanon (etonogestrel implant) may cause irregular or prolonged bleeding and is not considered a standard treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding.

###Answer:

Rationale:  
External cephalic version (ECV) is carried out to turn a non-cephalic fetus—most commonly a breech fetus—into the cephalic presentation. Thus a complete breech (or frank breech) position is actually the main indication for attempting ECV, not a contraindication.

• Previous caesarean-section scar – risk of scar dehiscence/rupture.  
• Twin (multiple) pregnancy – manipulation of one fetus endangers the other.  
• Placenta praevia – manipulation may provoke severe bleeding.  
• Ruptured membranes – less amniotic fluid and higher cord/compression risks.

A: The anterior fontanelle is diamond shaped.
B: The sutures of the vault are soft unossified membranes.

D: The occipito-mental diameter is normally too large to pass through the maternal pelvis.
E: Moulding of the fetal skull is a normal physiological process.

###Question: Considering the fetal skull, the following are true except?

A.  The anterior fontanelle is diamond shaped.
B.  The sutures of the vault are soft unossified membranes.
C.  The vertex presentation longitudinal diameter is sub-occipito-frontal diameter.
D.  The occipito-mental diameter is normally too large to pass through the maternal pelvis.
E.  Moulding of the fetal skull is a normal physiological process.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C

Rationale  
A. True – The anterior fontanelle (bregma) is characteristically diamond-shaped.  
B. True – The cranial sutures of the vault consist of soft, unossified membranous tissue that permits mobility of the skull bones.  
C. False – In a normal, well-flexed vertex presentation the engaging antero-posterior (longitudinal) diameter is the sub-occipito-bregmatic (≈ 9.5 cm), not the sub-occipito-frontal (≈ 10 cm).  
D. True – The occipito-mental diameter (≈ 12.5–13 cm), encountered in brow presentation, exceeds the obstetric dimensions of the maternal pelvis and therefore cannot normally pass through it.  
E. True – Moulding, the overlapping of the fetal skull bones during labour, is a normal physiological adaptation that reduces the presenting diameters.

Correct option: C. Insulin resistance

Rationale:
Secondary (endocrine) hypertension is classically associated with disorders in which excess or deficiency of specific hormones directly alters vascular tone, sodium balance, or cardiac output. Well-recognized endocrine causes include:

• Hyperthyroidism – increases cardiac output and pulse pressure, causing predominantly systolic hypertension.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Visual loss

Rationale: In-utero exposure to carbimazole (or its active metabolite methimazole) can produce a recognisable pattern of malformations—“carbimazole/methimazole embryopathy.” Characteristic defects include:
• Choanal or oesophageal atresia/tracheo-oesophageal fistula  
• Aplasia cutis congenita (most often on the scalp)  
• Nipple abnormalities such as athelia or hypoplastic nipples  
• Other mid-line or gastrointestinal defects (e.g., omphalocele)

Visual loss is not part of this well-described spectrum, so it is the option that is not a typical feature of carbimazole embryopathy.

B.  1 or 2 both parents with clinically diagnosed familiar hypercholesterolemia
C.  Positive genetic test for PCSK9
D.  Autosomal recessive FH

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D.  Autosomal recessive FH  

Rationale:  
• Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HoFH) results when a person inherits two LDL-receptor–affecting mutations (LDLR, APOB, PCSK9, etc.). Although two mutant alleles are present, the disorder still comes from genes that are classically transmitted in an autosomal-dominant (codominant) fashion; HoFH is therefore not classified as an autosomal-recessive disease.  
• Diagnostic clues for HoFH include very high LDL-C (typically ≥ 500 mg/dL untreated or ≥ 300 mg/dL while on therapy), the presence of xanthomas in childhood, parents with HeFH, and/or identification of biallelic pathogenic variants (LDLR, APOB, PCSK9).  
• Thus statements A, B and C describe accepted clinical/genetic criteria, whereas statement D is false.

question: A 6-week old infant presents with a two-week history of non-passage of stools. Abdominal examination reveals a uniformly distended abdomen with an empty rectum. The most likely diagnosis is:
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: A 6-week old infant presents with a two-week history of non-passage of stools. Abdominal examination reveals a uniformly distended abdomen with an empty rectum. The most likely diagnosis is:



###Options:
A.  Congenital pyloric stenosis
B.  Overfeeding
C.  Hirchsprung disease
D.  Intussusception

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Hirschsprung disease

Rationale:
Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon) is characterized by absence of ganglion cells in the distal bowel, leading to functional obstruction. Typical findings include:

• Delayed passage or complete absence of meconium/stool.  
• Progressive, uniform abdominal distension.  
• Rectal examination revealing an empty rectum; withdrawal of the finger may produce an explosive release of gas/stool.

The infant in the vignette has a 2-week history of no stools, a uniformly distended abdomen, and an empty rectum—classic for Hirschsprung disease. 

Congenital pyloric stenosis (A) presents with projectile, non-bilious vomiting, not stool obstruction. Overfeeding (B) causes regurgitation and colic but not prolonged absence of stool with distension. Intussusception (D) typically presents with episodic colicky pain and “currant jelly” stools rather than a persistent empty rectum.

question: A common cause of hypopituitarism in Developing Countries include
D: Severe blood loss during child birth

A.  Sarcoidosis
B.  Tuberculosis
C.  Surgery
D.  Severe blood loss during child birth

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Severe blood loss during child birth

Rationale: In many developing countries postpartum hemorrhage is still a frequent obstetric complication. Massive blood loss and resulting hypotension can cause ischemic necrosis of the anterior pituitary (Sheehan’s syndrome). This leads to varying degrees of anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies—i.e., hypopituitarism. While sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, and neurosurgical procedures can also involve the pituitary, postpartum hemorrhage remains one of the most common and characteristic causes of hypopituitarism in resource-limited settings.

Rationale: Measles produces transient but profound immune suppression that predisposes patients to respiratory super-infections. question: Which of the following is not a feature of acute severe asthma?

C.  Tachycardia
D.  Reduced forced expiratory volume in 1-second

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Fluent uninterrupted speech  

Rationale:  
Acute severe asthma is characterized by marked airway obstruction, leading to significant respiratory compromise. Key clinical findings include:  
• Difficulty speaking; patients can usually utter only words or short phrases, not fluent, uninterrupted speech.  
• Tachycardia (heart rate >110 beats/min).  
• Pulsus paradoxus (>10–12 mm Hg fall in systolic BP during inspiration).  
• Markedly reduced airflow measurements such as FEV₁ or peak expiratory flow (<40% of predicted or personal best).  

Therefore, fluent uninterrupted speech is not a feature of acute severe asthma.

###Answer:

Rationale:  
Severe Plasmodium falciparum infection produces age-related patterns of complications. In young children the common manifestations include severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia, acidosis/respiratory distress and jaundice due to massive haemolysis, so hyperbilirubinaemia is frequently encountered.

Therefore, in a 2-year-old child with falciparum malaria the most likely accompanying abnormality is hyperbilirubinaemia.

question: Which is NOT a cause of Hypercalcemia due to high bone turnover
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: Which is NOT a cause of Hypercalcemia due to high bone turnover 

###Options:
A.  Milk-alkali syndrome
B.  Immobilization
C.  frusemide use
D.  Hyperparathyroidism

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Milk-alkali syndrome  

Rationale  
Hypercalcaemia that results from high skeletal turnover is produced by conditions that accelerate bone resorption, such as immobilisation, primary hyperparathyroidism (via its osteoclastic effect) and similar states.  

• Immobilisation → rapid osteoclastic bone loss.  
• Hyperparathyroidism → PTH-driven osteoclastic activity and bone turnover.  
• Frusemide (furosemide) does not raise serum calcium; it increases renal calcium excretion and is actually used to treat hypercalcaemia, so it clearly is not a “high bone-turnover” cause.  

Milk-alkali (calcium-alkali) syndrome, however, produces hypercalcaemia through excessive gastrointestinal calcium absorption combined with decreased renal excretion, not through enhanced bone resorption. Therefore it is not a cause of hypercalcaemia due to high bone turnover.

C.  Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn

###Answer:

Rationale:  
• TTN is seen in term or near-term infants and is characterized by tachypnea and mild respiratory distress that appears soon after birth, reaches its peak within the first few hours, and typically improves or resolves within 24-48 hours as the fetal lung fluid is absorbed.

The other options are less likely:  
• Meconium aspiration syndrome and congenital pneumonia usually produce more severe, persistent distress and oxygen requirement.  
• Respiratory distress syndrome is primarily a disease of preterm infants and does not resolve so quickly.

Therefore, Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn is the most likely diagnosis.

question: A newborn baby at the first minute of life appears blue in the limbs but pink in the trunk, has a heart rate of 80/minute, has a weak grimace, a partial flexion of the limbs and irregular respiration. The most important immediate resuscitative measure at that moment is:

###Question: A newborn baby at the first minute of life appears blue in the limbs but pink in the trunk, has a heart rate of 80/minute, has a weak grimace, a partial flexion of the limbs and irregular respiration. The most important immediate resuscitative measure at that moment is:

B.  Set up 10% Dextrose-in-Water infusion
C.  Start bag and mask ventilation
D.  Start endotracheal intubation

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Start bag and mask ventilation

Rationale:
The 1-minute Apgar score is 5 (color 1, heart rate 1, reflex irritability 1, tone 1, respiration 1). According to neonatal resuscitation guidelines, any newborn with a heart rate below 100 beats/minute and/or inadequate respirations should receive positive-pressure ventilation. Bag-and-mask ventilation is the first-line method. Endotracheal intubation is reserved for cases where bag-mask ventilation fails or the heart rate remains <60 beats/minute. Warming and glucose infusion are supportive but do not address the immediate problem of bradycardia and inadequate breathing.

question: A 6-year old child presents with frequent passage of large volume of urine with excessive thirst. His urine shows glycosuria and the random blood glucose reads 14.8mmol/l. Which of the following conditions may be associated with the child’s condition?

###Question: A 6-year old child presents with frequent passage of large volume of urine with excessive thirst. His urine shows glycosuria and the random blood glucose reads 14.8mmol/l. Which of the following conditions may be associated with the child’s condition?
###Options:
A.  Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
B.  Grave’s disease
C.  Addison’s disease
D.  Hashimoto Thyroiditis

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Addison’s disease  

Rationale:  
The child’s polyuria, polydipsia, glycosuria and random blood glucose of 14.8 mmol/L are typical for type 1 diabetes mellitus, an autoimmune disorder caused by destruction of pancreatic β-cells. Type 1 diabetes commonly coexists with other autoimmune endocrinopathies as part of the autoimmune poly-glandular syndromes. Addison’s disease (autoimmune primary adrenal insufficiency) is one of the classic disorders that cluster with type 1 diabetes (Schmidt/autoimmune poly-glandular syndrome type 2). Systemic lupus erythematosus is not characteristically linked, while Graves’ disease or Hashimoto thyroiditis may occur but are less strongly linked in childhood than Addison’s disease.

question: All are primary function of Parathyroid hormone except.
B: Increasing reabsorption of calcium in kidney
D: Stimulate activation of Vit D in kidneys.
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: All are primary function of Parathyroid hormone except.

###Options:
A.  Stimulating bone resorption
B.  Increasing reabsorption of calcium in kidney
C.  Increase renal phosphate reabsorption
D.  Stimulate activation of Vit D in kidneys.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Increase renal phosphate reabsorption

Rationale:  
Parathyroid hormone (PTH) raises plasma calcium levels by:

• Stimulating bone resorption, releasing both Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ from bone (Option A).  
• Increasing distal tubular reabsorption of calcium in the kidney (Option B).  
• Activating renal 1-α-hydroxylase, which converts 25-OH-vitamin D to its active form, 1,25-(OH)₂-vitamin D₃ (Option D).

In the kidney, PTH actually decreases, not increases, phosphate reabsorption in the proximal tubule, causing phosphaturia. Therefore, “Increase renal phosphate reabsorption” is not a primary action of PTH, making Option C the exception.

###Options:
A.  Encephalitis
B.  Apnea
C.  Bronchopneumonia
D.  Rectal prolapse

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Bronchopneumonia  

Rationale:  
The most frequent complication of pertussis in infants and young children is secondary bacterial pneumonia (bronchopneumonia). It often develops after the initial catarrhal and paroxysmal stages and therefore may be first identified during subsequent follow-up visits when the child is re-examined or if new respiratory symptoms appear.  

• Encephalitis (A) is a very rare complication and would usually present acutely.  
• Apnea (B) occurs during the acute paroxysmal phase, not weeks later at follow-up.  
• Rectal prolapse (D) can result from forceful coughing but is much less common than pneumonia.  

Thus, bronchopneumonia is the condition most likely to be detected on follow-up after an episode of pertussis.

question: A two-year old child presents at the emergency unit with a 5-day history of cough, breathlessness, central cyanosis and a tender 6cm liver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: A two-year old child presents at the emergency unit with a 5-day history of cough, breathlessness, central cyanosis and a tender 6cm liver. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

###Options:
A.  Eisenmenger’s syndrome
B.  Bronchial asthma
C.  Pertussis
D.  Pneumonia with cardiac failure (X)

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Pneumonia with cardiac failure

Rationale:
• The 5-day history of cough and increasing breathlessness points to an acute respiratory infection such as pneumonia.  
• Central cyanosis indicates significant hypoxaemia, a common complication of severe pneumonia.  
• A tender, enlarged liver (6 cm below the costal margin) in an acutely ill child is classic for acute right-sided heart failure/congestive cardiac failure. In young children, severe pneumonia frequently precipitates heart failure because hypoxia and acidosis increase pulmonary vascular resistance and workload on the right heart.  
• Eisenmenger’s syndrome (A) causes chronic, not acute, cyanosis and hepatomegaly is usually non-tender.  
• Bronchial asthma (B) causes episodic wheeze; hepatomegaly is not a typical feature.  
• Pertussis (C) causes paroxysmal coughing spells but does not produce tender hepatomegaly or congestive signs.  

Thus, the constellation of acute respiratory infection, cyanosis, and tender hepatomegaly is best explained by pneumonia complicated by cardiac failure.

question: A 3-year old on treatment for a heart disease presents with serum bicarbonate 14.2mmol/l. The clinical picture that matches this laboratory result is:

###Question: A 3-year old on treatment for a heart disease presents with serum bicarbonate 14.2mmol/l. The clinical picture that matches this laboratory result is: 
###Options:
A.  Fast breathing
B.  Inability to stand erect
C.  Muscle stiffness
D.  Hyperactive bowel sounds

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Fast breathing

Rationale:  
A serum bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) level of 14.2 mmol/L is well below the normal range (≈ 22–26 mmol/L) and signifies metabolic acidosis. The immediate physiologic compensation for metabolic acidosis is respiratory: the medullary respiratory center drives hyperventilation (Kussmaul respirations) to lower PaCO₂ and raise pH toward normal. Clinically this appears as rapid, often deep breathing.  
• Inability to stand erect, muscle stiffness, and hyperactive bowel sounds are not characteristic compensatory manifestations of metabolic acidosis.

question: Which of the following is not a cause of hypercalcaemia
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: Which of the following is not a cause of hypercalcaemia


###Options:
A.  Primary hyperparathyroidism
B.  Malignancy
C.  Sarcoidosis
D.  Hypothyroidism

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Hypothyroidism

Rationale:
• Primary hyperparathyroidism (A) increases PTH secretion, raising serum calcium—commonest outpatient cause of hypercalcaemia.  
• Malignancy (B) causes hypercalcaemia via bone metastases, osteolytic cytokines or PTH-related peptide—commonest inpatient cause.  
• Sarcoidosis (C) and other granulomatous diseases produce extra-renal 1-α-hydroxylase activity, increasing calcitriol and intestinal calcium absorption.  
• Hypothyroidism (D) is not a recognized cause of hypercalcaemia; in contrast, hyperthyroidism can cause mild hypercalcaemia due to increased bone turnover, while hypothyroidism is more often associated with low–normal calcium levels.

Therefore, option D is the exception.

Chronic use of systemic glucocorticoids suppresses osteoblastic activity, enhances osteoclastic bone resorption, reduces intestinal calcium absorption, and increases renal calcium loss. Rationale:  
The Moro (startle) reflex is elicited in newborns by a sudden loud noise or abrupt change in position. It is characterized by a stereotyped, sequential motor response:

• Placing reflex: stroking the dorsum of the foot against the edge of a table leads the infant to flex then extend the leg to “place” the foot.  

Therefore, the observed sequence is the Moro reflex.

question: A 21-day old infant who has been fed infant formula from birth presents with repeated blinking and lip smacking. There was no fever or jaundice. The most likely aetiological factor is:

###Question: A 21-day old infant who has been fed infant formula from birth presents with repeated blinking and lip smacking. There was no fever or jaundice. The most likely aetiological factor is:

###Options:
A.  Perinatal asphyxia
B.  Hypoglycaemia
C.  Hypocalcaemia
D.  Brain tumour

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Hypocalcaemia  

Rationale:  
Late-onset neonatal hypocalcaemia typically appears after the first week of life and is classically precipitated by feeding with cow-milk–based formulas, which contain a high phosphate load. The elevated serum phosphate drives calcium into tissues, producing symptomatic hypocalcaemia. Seizures in this age group are often “subtle,” presenting as repeated blinking, lip smacking, chewing or other automatisms, exactly as described.  

• Perinatal asphyxia and hypoglycaemia usually cause seizures within the first 24–72 hours of life, not at 3 weeks.  
• Brain tumours are exceedingly rare in neonates and would more likely produce focal neurological deficits or raised ICP signs.  

Hence, hypocalcaemia is the most probable aetiology.

• Other listed procedures (cystoscopy, hysteroscopy, hysterosalpingography) visualize the bladder, uterine cavity, or tubal patency indirectly and cannot reliably confirm a tubal ectopic pregnancy.  
Therefore, laparoscopy is considered the gold standard diagnostic tool.

question: Polyhydramnios is associated with the following except:
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: Polyhydramnios is associated with the following except:




###Options:
A.  Maternal diabetes
B.  Spina bifida
C.  Maternal non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
D.  Omphalocele
E.  Chorioangioma of the placenta

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Maternal non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

Rationale:
• Polyhydramnios results from either increased production of amniotic fluid (e.g., fetal polyuria) or impaired fetal swallowing/absorption.  
• Conditions classically linked to polyhydramnios include:  
  – Maternal diabetes mellitus → fetal hyperglycaemia and osmotic diuresis.  
  – Open neural-tube/CNS defects such as anencephaly and spina bifida → impaired swallowing.  
  – Anterior abdominal-wall defects such as omphalocele → loss of fluid into the sac and impaired gastrointestinal function.  
  – Large placental tumours such as chorioangioma → increased fetal cardiac output and polyuria.  
• In contrast, maternal NSAIDs (e.g., indomethacin) inhibit fetal renal prostaglandin synthesis, reduce fetal urine output and are actually used therapeutically to reduce excessive amniotic fluid. They are therefore associated with oligohydramnios, not polyhydramnios.

Hence option C is the exception.

question: The following are complications of multiple pregnancy except?
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: The following are complications of multiple pregnancy except?

###Options:
A.  Placenta praevia.
B.  Diabetes mellitus.
C.  Pre-eclampsia
D.  Malpresentation
E.  Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR).

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Placenta praevia.

Rationale:
Multiple (twin or higher‐order) pregnancies are characteristically associated with:
• Gestational diabetes mellitus – because of the larger placental mass and higher levels of diabetogenic hormones.  
• Hypertensive disorders, especially pre-eclampsia – incidence is two- to three-fold higher than in singleton pregnancies.  
• Malpresentation – crowding in the uterus means one or both fetuses are frequently breech, transverse, or compound.  
• Intra-uterine growth restriction (IUGR) – sharing the uterine and placental environment predisposes to growth discordance and overall growth restriction.

An increased risk of placenta praevia is not considered a typical or consistent complication attributable to multiple gestation; the main risk factors for placenta praevia are previous caesarean section, uterine surgery, multiparity, advancing maternal age, and smoking. Therefore, among the options listed, placenta praevia is the exception.

question: A 5-week old boy and first child of the family presents with recurrent projectile vomiting after feeds, which started two weeks prior to presentation. On examination he appears moderately dehydrated with a palpable almond-shaped mass in the epigastrium immediately after suckling. The most likely diagnosis is:

###Question: A 5-week old boy and first child of the family presents with recurrent projectile vomiting after feeds, which started two weeks prior to presentation. On examination he appears moderately dehydrated with a palpable almond-shaped mass in the epigastrium immediately after suckling. The most likely diagnosis is: 
###Options:
A.  Congenital pyloric stenosis
B.  Duodenal atresia.
C.  Haemolytic uraemic syndrome
D.  Intussusception

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Congenital pyloric stenosis

Rationale: 
• Age and onset – Hypertrophic (congenital) pyloric stenosis typically presents in the 2-6-week-old infant with progressive, non-bilious projectile vomiting after feeds.  
• Physical findings – A firm, olive/almond-shaped mass palpable in the epigastrium/right upper quadrant immediately after feeding is classic for pyloric stenosis.  
• Associated dehydration – Repeated vomiting leads to fluid loss and signs of dehydration, which fits the clinical picture.  
• Other options do not match:  
  – Duodenal atresia usually manifests on the first day of life with bilious vomiting and a “double bubble” sign, not at 3-5 weeks.  
  – Haemolytic uraemic syndrome presents with haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia and renal failure, not projectile vomiting.  
  – Intussusception typically occurs later (6-18 months) with intermittent abdominal pain, “currant-jelly” stools and a sausage-shaped mass, not an olive-like epigastric mass.

Therefore, congenital pyloric stenosis is the most likely diagnosis.

question: By means of real time ultrasound examination
A: Pregnancy can usually be detected 5 weeks after the last menstrual period
B: The fetal heart cannot be seen until 10 weeks after the last period
C: Placental praevia can be readily demonstrated after the 16th week of pregnancy
D: The biparietal diameter can be measured reliably after the 12th week of pregnancy
E: A reliable estimate of gestational age can be made in the 3rd trimester
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: By means of real time ultrasound examination
	
  
	 
	 
	

###Options:
A.  Pregnancy can usually be detected 5 weeks after the last menstrual period
B.  The fetal heart cannot be seen until 10 weeks after the last period
C.  Placental praevia can be readily demonstrated after the 16th week of pregnancy
D.  The biparietal diameter can be measured reliably after the 12th week of pregnancy
E.  A reliable estimate of gestational age can be made in the 3rd trimester

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct options: A and D  

Rationale  
A. Pregnancy can usually be detected 5 weeks after the last menstrual period – With modern real-time ultrasound (especially transvaginal), a gestational sac is typically visible by 4½–5 weeks LMP, so detection at 5 weeks is entirely feasible.  

B. The fetal heart cannot be seen until 10 weeks after the last period – Incorrect. Cardiac activity is normally demonstrable on real-time (TVS) scanning from about 6–7 weeks LMP.  

C. Placenta praevia can be readily demonstrated after the 16th week – Although placental position can be imaged this early, its relationship to the internal os often changes as the lower uterine segment develops; therefore a reliable diagnosis of placenta praevia is not made until much later (around 28–32 weeks).  

D. The biparietal diameter can be measured reliably after the 12th week of pregnancy – True. From 12–13 weeks onward, BPD is easily visualised and gives a reproducible measurement for dating and growth assessment.  

E. A reliable estimate of gestational age can be made in the 3rd trimester – Accuracy of dating falls as pregnancy advances (±3 weeks or more in the 3rd trimester), so it is not considered reliable then.

question: The following are absolute indication for caesarean section
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: The following are absolute indication for caesarean section 
	 
	  
	 
	 
###Options:
A.  Hydrocephalus
B.  Type IV placenta praevia
C.  Abruption placentae
D.  Previous multiple caesarean section
E.  Previous classical caesarean section

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct options: B, D and E  

Rationale  
Absolute (unconditional) indications for caesarean section are situations in which vaginal delivery is considered unsafe for mother and/or fetus under any circumstances.  
• Type IV (major/central) placenta praevia (option B) – the placenta completely covers the internal os; labour or artificial rupture of membranes will cause torrential haemorrhage, so Caesarean section is mandatory.  
• Previous multiple lower-segment caesarean sections (option D) – with two or more scars the risk of uterine rupture rises markedly; most centres regard this as an absolute indication for elective repeat Caesarean.  
• Previous classical (vertical uterine) caesarean section (option E) – the scar runs through the contractile upper segment and is highly prone to rupture in labour; therefore a repeat Caesarean is obligatory.

Hydrocephalus (option A) can often be managed by decompression of the fetal head or by assisted vaginal delivery, so it is not an absolute indication.  
In abruption placentae (option C) the preferred route of delivery depends on maternal/fetal condition and cervical status; many cases can be delivered vaginally, hence it is not an absolute indication.

###Question: A 3-year old child presents with fever, progressively worsening cough and difficulty with breathing. Physical examination reveals an acutely ill child with axillary temperature of 37.8⁰C, loud grunts, chest wall retraction, reduced chest movement, reduced vocal resonance and breath sounds. ###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Pneumonia with pleural effusion  

Rationale:  
• The child has fever, cough and respiratory distress, pointing to an infectious pulmonary process.  
• Physical signs of pleural effusion include asymmetrical or reduced chest movement on the affected side, diminished/absent breath sounds, and decreased vocal resonance—all of which are described.  
• Grunting is a compensatory mechanism seen in severe parenchymal disease (e.g., pneumonia) and when effusion compromises ventilation.  
• Upper-airway disorders such as acute epiglottitis or laryngotracheobronchitis typically produce stridor, hoarseness or barking cough, not markedly diminished breath sounds over the lungs.  
• Foreign-body aspiration usually presents with sudden onset symptoms and focal wheeze rather than the progressive course with systemic signs seen here.  

Hence, pneumonia complicated by pleural effusion best explains the findings.

Option C shows entirely normal glucose and HbA1c values.  
Option D has an HbA1c of 7.5 %, also diagnostic of diabetes.

Therefore, option A best defines pre-diabetes in this patient.

The Random Blood Glucose is 380mg/dl, urinalysis shows glucose (+++), ketones (++) and proteins (+) while serum electrolytes show bicarbonate level of 10mmol/l and potassium level of 2.7mmol/l. C: Intravenous infusion of Half-Strength Darrow’s Solution.

###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: A 13-year old girl presents at CHER with Glasgow Coma Score of 6/15. The Random Blood Glucose is 380mg/dl, urinalysis shows glucose (+++), ketones (++) and proteins (+) while serum electrolytes show bicarbonate level of 10mmol/l and potassium level of 2.7mmol/l. The important immediate step in the management of the child is:

###Options:
A.  Intravenous infusion of Normal Saline.
B.  Intravenous administration of Sodium bicarbonate.
C.  Intravenous infusion of Half-Strength Darrow’s Solution.
D.  Intravenous administration of Ceftriaxone.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A.  Intravenous infusion of Normal Saline.

Rationale:
The child has diabetic ketoacidosis (marked hyperglycaemia, ketonuria, severe metabolic acidosis with bicarbonate 10 mmol/L) and is obtunded (GCS 6). The first and most urgent priority in DKA is restoration of intravascular volume to improve perfusion, renal function and clearance of glucose/ketones, and to allow subsequent safe insulin and potassium therapy. Isotonic 0.9 % saline is the recommended initial fluid. 

• Sodium bicarbonate (option B) is not routinely indicated in DKA and is reserved for extreme acidosis (pH < 6.9) because it can worsen hypokalaemia and increase risk of cerebral oedema.  
• Half-strength Darrow’s solution (option C) is hypotonic and contraindicated in the initial resuscitation phase.  
• Ceftriaxone (option D) may be required later if infection is suspected, but it is not the immediate life-saving step.

Therefore, prompt intravenous normal saline is the correct immediate intervention.

question: The most common cause of hypothyroidism
model_prompt:

###Question: The most common cause of hypothyroidism


###Options:
A.  Congenital hypothyroidism
B.  Hashimoto's disease
C.  Radiation treatment of the thyroid.
D.  Thyroiditis

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: B. Hashimoto's disease

Rationale:  
In iodine-sufficient populations, the vast majority of acquired hypothyroidism is due to chronic autoimmune (Hashimoto) thyroiditis. The immune-mediated destruction of thyroid tissue gradually reduces hormone production, making it the leading overall cause of hypothyroidism in adults. Congenital hypothyroidism (A) refers to thyroid hormone deficiency present at birth, radiation-induced hypothyroidism (C) occurs only in individuals who have received therapeutic or environmental radiation to the neck, and subacute or silent thyroiditis (D) are less common and usually transient causes.

question: The following feature of Graves’ disease differentiate from other causes of hyperthyroidism
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: The following feature of Graves’ disease differentiate from other causes of hyperthyroidism 

###Options:
A.  Weight loss and increase appetite
B.  Heat intolerance
C.  Diffuse goitre
D.  Systolic hypertension

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Diffuse goitre

Rationale:
Most clinical manifestations of thyrotoxicosis—weight loss with increased appetite, heat intolerance, and a hyperdynamic circulation that can produce systolic hypertension—occur in virtually all causes of hyper-thyroidism.  
What sets Graves’ disease apart is that the autoimmune stimulation of the entire thyroid gland by TSH-receptor antibodies produces a diffusely enlarged, vascular (“diffuse”) goitre, whereas other common aetiologies (toxic multinodular goitre, toxic adenoma, thyroiditis, exogenous thyroxine) either show nodularity, a solitary nodule, a tender gland, or no enlargement at all. Therefore a diffuse goitre is the distinguishing feature among the options given.

D.  Hypersecretory thyroid carcinoma

###Answer:
outputs:

Rationale:  
Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder in which thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins activate the TSH receptor, leading to diffuse goitre and excess production of thyroid hormones (thyroxine and triiodothyronine). It accounts for roughly 60–80 % of all cases of hyperthyroidism, making it by far the most common etiologic entity. Acute thyroiditis can cause transient thyrotoxicosis but is far less frequent, TSH-secreting pituitary adenomas are rare (<1 % of hyperthyroidism), and hypersecretory thyroid carcinoma is an exceptional cause.

question: Which of the following is not a feature of nutritional rickets?

###Question: Which of the following is not a feature of nutritional rickets?
###Options:
A.  Wide sandal gap
B.  Genu recurvatum
C.  Kyphosis
D.  Harrison sulcus

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Wide sandal gap

Rationale:
Nutritional (vitamin-D-deficiency) rickets produces characteristic skeletal changes caused by softened, demineralised bone. Typical bone deformities include:

• Genu varum, genu valgum and sometimes genu recurvatum (knee hyper-extension)
• Spinal curvature abnormalities such as kyphosis or kyphoscoliosis
• Thoracic changes such as the rachitic rosary and Harrison sulcus

A “wide sandal gap” (increased space between the first and second toes) is classically associated with chromosomal disorders such as Down syndrome and is not a recognized manifestation of nutritional rickets.

question: Ante-partum haemorrhage
A: Is defined as “bleeding from the genital tract in pregnancy”
D: May be caused by carcinoma insitu of the cervix

You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: 	Ante-partum haemorrhage
	  
	
	
	

###Options:
A.  Is defined as “bleeding from the genital tract in pregnancy”
B.  May be complicated by hypofibrinogenaemia
C.  Requires assessment by vaginal examination
D.  May be caused by carcinoma insitu of the cervix
E.  Is always painless.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct options:  B and D

Rationale  

A. False – Ante-partum haemorrhage is classically defined as bleeding from the genital tract AFTER 20–24 (UK) or 28 (WHO) weeks’ gestation and before the onset of labour. The wording “in pregnancy” is too broad and would include first-trimester bleeding, so it does not meet the accepted definition.  

B. True – Abruption placentae, one of the common causes of APH, releases thromboplastins that can trigger consumptive coagulopathy, leading to hypofibrinogenaemia and DIC.  

C. False – A digital vaginal examination must not be performed until placenta praevia has been ruled out (usually by ultrasound) because it can precipitate torrential bleeding.  

D. True – Although the main obstetric causes are placenta praevia and placental abruption, bleeding from local genital tract lesions (e.g., cervical ectropion, cervicitis, invasive or in-situ carcinoma of the cervix, vulvo-vaginal varices) can present as APH.  

E. False – Placenta praevia typically causes painless bleeding, but placental abruption is usually accompanied by abdominal pain and uterine tenderness; therefore APH is not always painless.

question: A 5-year old who has had persistent diarrhoea has serum potassium of 2.5 mmol/L. Which of the following clinical manifestations is expected as a result of the dyselectrolytaemia?
model_prompt:
###Instruction: The following are multiple choice questions (MCQs).
You should directly answer the question by choosing the correct option and then provide a rationale for your answer. 

###Question: A 5-year old who has had persistent diarrhoea has serum potassium of 2.5 mmol/L. Which of the following clinical manifestations is expected as a result of the dyselectrolytaemia?
###Options:
A.  Positive Chvostek’s sign
B.  Scaphoid abdomen
C.  Abdominal distension
D.  Fast, deep breathing

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: C. Abdominal distension

Rationale:  
Serum potassium of 2.5 mmol/L indicates marked hypokalaemia. Potassium is essential for normal smooth-muscle excitability; when it is low, gastrointestinal smooth muscle becomes atonic, predisposing to paralytic ileus. Clinically this presents with abdominal distension, decreased bowel sounds and sometimes vomiting.  

• Positive Chvostek’s sign (Option A) is characteristic of hypocalcaemia, not hypokalaemia.  
• A scaphoid (sunken) abdomen (Option B) is seen in states such as severe malnutrition or intra-abdominal perforation with peritonitis, not in ileus caused by low potassium.

question: Which of the following vaccines is effective in the prevention of neonatal tetanus?

B.  Anti-Tetanus serum
C.  Measles
D.  Tetanus toxoid

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: D. Tetanus toxoid

Rationale:
Neonatal tetanus occurs when an unimmunized (or inadequately immunized) mother passes no protective tetanus antibodies to her newborn; infection then follows contamination of the umbilical stump. The proven preventive measure is active immunization of the mother during pregnancy (or women of child-bearing age) with tetanus toxoid–containing vaccine, which induces maternal IgG antibodies that cross the placenta and protect the neonate for the first few weeks of life. Neither anti-tetanus serum (passive antibody given to treat or temporarily prevent tetanus), measles vaccine, nor the infant pentavalent doses can provide this critical transplacental protection before birth. Therefore, tetanus toxoid is the vaccine specifically effective in preventing neonatal tetanus.

Rationale:
A mature (benign) cystic teratoma is the commonest ovarian tumour in women of reproductive age. It arises from totipotential germ cells and therefore can contain differentiated tissue from all three germ layers—commonly hair, sebaceous material, bone and teeth. On ultrasound or CT/MRI a tooth or other calcified bony element within a complex, partly solid ovarian mass is virtually pathognomonic.

• Dysgerminoma – solid germ-cell malignancy, usually homogeneous.  
• Serous or mucinous cystadenoma – usually purely cystic without calcified teeth.  
• Brenner tumour – solid epithelial tumour, rarely contains teeth.  
• “Meigs tumour” (fibroma with ascites and hydrothorax) – solid, fibrous, not tooth-containing.

Therefore the description best fits a mature teratoma.

In women with underlying heart disease the greatest haemodynamic stress is not during mid-pregnancy but at the time of and immediately after delivery. Once the baby and placenta are expelled there is a sudden “autotransfusion” of 500–800 mL of blood from the emptied uterus into the maternal circulation, the inferior vena-caval obstruction caused by the gravid uterus is relieved, and systemic vascular resistance rises. These rapid changes sharply increase venous return and cardiac work; if myocardial reserve is limited, acute left-sided failure, pulmonary oedema and fatal arrhythmias are most likely to develop. Consequently the majority of cardiac decompensations and maternal deaths in heart disease occur in the first 24–48 hours after delivery—i.e., in the early postpartum period.

• The triad of high fever, passage of dark (“coca-cola”/“blackwater”) urine, and sudden profound anaemia (haematocrit 12 %) is characteristic of severe falciparum malaria with haemoglobinuria.

• Acute glomerulonephritis typically presents with cola-coloured urine due to haematuria, but the urine discoloration lasts longer and severe anaemia, massive splenomegaly, and jaundice are not prominent.  
• Septicaemia and viral hepatitis can give fever and hepatomegaly, but they do not usually cause the striking haemolysis, severe anaemia and black urine seen here.

Therefore, severe falciparum malaria is the most likely diagnosis.

• Metastatic neuroblastoma can give bilateral proptosis, but it does not produce a preceding leukocoria in the eye.  

Therefore, the history of leukocoria followed by severe bilateral proptosis in a 3-year-old most strongly suggests disseminated retinoblastoma.

question: Regarding the pathology of concealed accidental haemorrhage, the following statement is true:
A: Blood is retained mainly due to compression by the fetal head
B: Couvelaire uterus is a term describing a uterus with a huge retro placental clot
C: The release of prostaglandins initiates the process of disseminated intravascular coagulopathy
D: Renal tubular necrosis is always reversible
E: Spasm and degenerative changes occur in the decidual arterioles due to associated preeclampsia

B.  Couvelaire uterus is a term describing a uterus with a huge retro placental clot
C.  The release of prostaglandins initiates the process of disseminated intravascular coagulopathy
D.  Renal tubular necrosis is always reversible
E.  Spasm and degenerative changes occur in the decidual arterioles due to associated preeclampsia

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: E  

Rationale:  
• Concealed accidental haemorrhage (concealed abruption placentae) is strongly associated with pre-eclampsia/hypertension. The basic vascular lesion is arteriolar spasm with fibrinoid degeneration and necrosis of the decidual (spiral) arterioles; this arteriopathy predisposes to bleeding behind the placenta.  

• A. Blood is retained chiefly because the placental margins remain adherent and the uterus is tonically contracted; obstruction by the fetal head is only one of several minor factors, so the statement is inaccurate.  

• B. A Couvelaire uterus (uterine apoplexy) refers to extravasation of blood into and through the myometrium producing a blue-violet serosal surface, not merely a large retro-placental clot.  

• C. Disseminated intravascular coagulation in abruption is initiated by thromboplastin (tissue factor) released from the damaged placenta/decidua, not by prostaglandins.  

• D. Acute tubular necrosis is usually—but not invariably—reversible; furthermore, cortical necrosis (which is irreversible) can also occur, so the word “always” makes the statement incorrect.

###Question: A 36 year- old woman presents with vaginal bleeding at 8 weeks 3 days’ gestation. She has never been pregnant before. The bright red ’spotting’ started 3 days ago with no abdominal pain. ###Options:

B.  Full blood count
C.  Urine pregnancy test
D.  Blood pregnancy test
E.  Chromosomal studies

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: A. Transvaginal ultrasound scan  

Rationale:  
First-trimester bleeding with a closed cervix is most commonly a threatened miscarriage. The key test to establish (a) that the pregnancy is intra-uterine and (b) whether the embryo is viable is a transvaginal ultrasound. It can demonstrate the gestational sac, yolk sac, embryo and—crucially—a fetal heartbeat, allowing differentiation between a viable threatened miscarriage and other causes of early bleeding (missed, incomplete or ectopic pregnancy).  

• A full blood count (B) may be useful if bleeding is heavy but does not confirm the diagnosis.  
• A urine pregnancy test (C) only tells if hCG is present and adds no information about viability or location.  
• A single quantitative serum hCG (D) confirms pregnancy but, without serial values, cannot reliably assess viability; even serial levels are less definitive than ultrasound once the gestational sac should be visible.  
• Chromosomal studies (E) are not part of the initial diagnostic work-up.  

Therefore, transvaginal ultrasound is the most helpful investigation in this scenario.

Which of the following is true regarding the blastocyst?
A: After implantation, it is surrounded by decidual parietalis
B: The cytotrophoblast lies outside the syncytiotrophoblast
C: The primary Villi are formed of cytotrophoblast only.
D: The secondary villi contain fetal blood vessels
E: The outer cell mass is formed of trophoblast

###Question: At ovulation, the ovulated egg is picked up by the fimbria of the fallopian tube and then swept by ciliary action towards the ampulla where fertilization occurs. As soon as the zygote is formed, it begins dividing very rapidly leading to the formation of a blastocyst.
Which of the following is true regarding the blastocyst?




 

###Options:
A.  After implantation, it is surrounded by decidual parietalis
B.  The cytotrophoblast lies outside the syncytiotrophoblast
C.  The primary Villi are formed of cytotrophoblast only.
D.  The secondary villi contain fetal blood vessels
E.  The outer cell mass is formed of trophoblast

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: E  

Rationale  
A  Decidua parietalis is the part of the endometrium remote from the implanted conceptus.  Immediately after implantation the blastocyst is embedded in decidua basalis (deep) and covered by decidua capsularis (superficial), not parietalis – so A is false.  

B  In the trophoblast the outer layer is the syncytiotrophoblast and the inner layer the cytotrophoblast; therefore cytotrophoblast is inside, not outside – B is false.  

C  Primary chorionic villi consist of a central core of cytotrophoblast covered by syncytiotrophoblast, so they are not “cytotrophoblast only” – C is false.  

D  Fetal blood vessels appear only when extra-embryonic mesoderm invades the villus to form tertiary villi; secondary villi have mesoderm but no vessels – D is false.  

E  At the blastocyst stage the cells are arranged in an inner cell mass (embryoblast) and an outer cell mass called the trophoblast; hence E is true.

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: E  

Rationale:  
Ante-partum haemorrhage is defined as bleeding from the genital tract after about 24 weeks’ gestation until delivery. Premature ovarian failure (primary ovarian insufficiency) is classically linked to a number of genetic, metabolic and autoimmune conditions:

• Autoimmune disorders – thyroiditis, Addison’s disease, polyglandular autoimmune syndromes frequently coexist with or cause ovarian failure.

question: Concerning placenta morphometry, which of this is not true
B: Weighs between 500-600gms or 1/6th of the baby weight
C: The syncytiotrophoblast leads the trophoblastic invasion
D: The nitabuchs layer is not well formed in mid trimester
E: The basal plate relates to the fetus and the chorionic plate with the mother

###Question: 

Concerning placenta morphometry, which of this is not true

A.  Has about 15-20 cotyledons
B.  Weighs between 500-600gms or 1/6th of the baby weight
C.  The syncytiotrophoblast leads the trophoblastic invasion
D.  The nitabuchs layer is not well formed in mid trimester
E.  The basal plate relates to the fetus and the chorionic plate with the mother

###Answer:
outputs:
Correct option: E

Rationale  
• The maternal surface of a term placenta is divided into about 15-20 lobulated areas called cotyledons – statement A is true.  
• A normal term placenta weighs roughly 500–600 g, i.e. about one-sixth of the newborn’s weight – statement B is true.  
• During early implantation the syncytiotrophoblast erodes the endometrium and therefore “leads” the initial trophoblastic invasion – statement C is true.  
• Nitabuch’s fibrinoid layer, situated between trophoblast and decidua basalis, begins to form in the second trimester and becomes more prominent toward term; hence it is not yet well formed in mid-trimester – statement D is true.  
• The basal plate is the maternal (decidual) side of the placenta, while the chorionic plate is the fetal side. Statement E reverses these relationships and is therefore NOT true.

Thus, option E is the incorrect statement.

A normal / “reactive” antenatal cardiotocograph (non-stress test) is defined by:
•  A baseline fetal heart rate within the normal range (commonly taken as about 110-160 bpm; many texts accept 120-160 bpm).

Hence statement C best describes the use of the vacuum extractor.
